title: the S-4 two-level copy and the S-5 request-id draw cost, measured on Linux
method: Both numerators are measured with the repository's canonical protocol (src/benchmarks/protocol.py::measure: warm up, collect, min-of-N inside a batch, then the median of the per-batch minima). The ORIGINAL S-4 and S-5 instruments are not in the repository, so this does not reproduce them: the old figures are quoted for comparison only and are neither re-measured nor re-derived. Each item is reported as a BEFORE/AFTER PAIR.

protocol.estimator: min-of-N inside a batch, then the median of the per-batch minima
protocol.the_original_instruments_are_not_committ: There is no S-4 or S-5 microbenchmark in src/benchmarks/ or scripts/. The old figures came from a hand-rolled Windows script, and the M-4 bead's own record lists as a defect it closed: 'single-shot min-of-N with no warmup instead of src/benchmarks/protocol.py::measure'. This script uses the canonical protocol and compares against the OLD published figures, not against a re-run of the old instrument.

s4_two_level_copy.what: copy.deepcopy against the production _two_level_copy, on the same auth payload

payload.description: one level deep, with one nested 'tier' whose values are all scalars - the shape assert_user_payload_shape admits, and the shape the two-level copy is an isomorphism of

s4_two_level_copy.numerator_is: the difference between the two arms on this payload

the_old_figure_for_comparison_only.host: Windows (the S-4 commit body said so itself)

s5_request_id_draw.what: the unconditional path before the change - THREE independent uuid4 draws, one per guard that used to mint its own id - against the ONE draw the memoisation leaves on that path
s5_request_id_draw.numerator_is: the cost of the two draws the change removed

denominator.uncontended_floor_source: GATE B's named floor; the committed corroboration is perf-results/RESULT-20261012-sweepB/sweepA_8_stats.csv (min 4.09577600294142 ms at concurrency 8)

what_is_not_asserted.no_new_less_old: No improvement is claimed and no arm is asserted to be the smaller one: the arms are compared for VACUITY only (they must not measure the same number). The before/after pair IS the numerator's own derivation, so it is reported as a pair.
what_is_not_asserted.the_old_figures_are_not_re_measured: The old S-4 and S-5 figures are quoted for comparison only. They were measured on other hosts with an instrument that is not in the repository, so they are neither re-measured nor re-derived, and the difference between the old and the new figures is a difference between INSTRUMENTS as well as between hosts.
what_is_not_asserted.not_an_endpoint_measurement: no request is issued and the app's lifespan is not run
what_is_not_asserted.the_payload_is_named: The S-4 figure is the cost on the payload named above; a different payload shape is a different figure.
what_is_not_asserted.main_json_stub_never_compared: tests/benchmarks/baselines/main.json is a stub and is never compared
